what_its_for: Inclisiran is used to lower your LDL cholesterol (sometimes called 'bad' cholesterol') in your blood. It is used along with a low-fat diet and other cholesterol-lowering medicines when diet and other treatments alone are not enough. It is prescribed for adults who have a condition called heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (an inherited condition that causes very high cholesterol) or who have heart disease and need extra help lowering their cholesterol.
how_to_take: Inclisiran is given as an injection under your skin (subcutaneous injection), usually in your belly area, upper arm, or thigh. It is NOT a shot you give yourself at home — your doctor, nurse, or other healthcare provider will give you this injection in a clinic or office setting. You should continue eating a heart-healthy, low-fat diet while taking this medicine.
dosing: Your first dose is given by your healthcare provider. Then you will get a second dose 3 months (about 90 days) later. After that, you will receive a dose every 6 months (twice a year). This every-6-month schedule means you only need 2 injections per year after your starting doses. Always keep your appointments so you do not miss your doses.
missed_dose: If you miss your scheduled injection appointment, contact your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to reschedule. Try not to delay too long. If you received a missed dose within 3 months of when it was due, your next dose will still be given on your original schedule. If it has been more than 3 months since your missed dose, your doctor will restart your dosing schedule. Do not try to give yourself this injection at home.
storage: Inclisiran is stored and handled by your healthcare provider or pharmacy — you do not need to store it at home. If for any reason you are given a prefilled syringe to bring to your appointment, keep it refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Do not freeze it. Keep it in the original carton to protect it from light. If kept at room temperature (up to 77°F / 25°C), it must be used within 6 months. Keep all medicines out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: There are no specific foods, drinks, or activities that you must strictly avoid while taking inclisiran. However, you should: avoid stopping your other prescribed cholesterol-lowering medicines (such as statins) unless your doctor tells you to; continue avoiding high-fat and high-cholesterol foods; avoid missing your scheduled injection appointments, as this medicine only works when given on time.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get medical help right away if you notice any of the following after your injection: signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing; severe pain, redness, swelling, or an open sore at the injection site; any unexpected or unusual symptoms. Also talk to your doctor before starting any new medicines, including over-the-counter drugs or supplements, and if you become pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
when_it_works: Inclisiran starts lowering your LDL cholesterol within a few weeks of your first injection. The full cholesterol-lowering effect is usually seen by the time of your second dose (around 3 months). Because this medicine works slowly and steadily, it is important to keep all of your follow-up appointments and lab tests so your doctor can check how well it is working for you. Do not stop treatment just because you feel fine — high cholesterol usually has no symptoms.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Inclisiran may harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. You should use effective birth control while taking this medicine and for at least 5 months after your last dose. Kidney or liver problems: If you have kidney or liver disease, tell your doctor. In most cases, no dose adjustment is needed, but your doctor will monitor you closely. Older adults (age 65 and over): This medicine can be used in older adults; no special dose change is usually needed. Children: Inclisiran is not approved for use in children under 18 years of age.
